findings.title: Janitor erases from the links map while iterating it, concurrently with other threads
findings.description: The janitor lambda walks store.all() (a std::map) and calls entries_.erase(it), which invalidates the iterator and yields undefined behavior. It also mutates the same Store and Cache concurrently with request handlers, warm_cache worker threads, and any other callers, with no synchronization at all. Interleaving: a handler inserts/resolves a link or a cache warm-up writes an entry while the janitor sweeps -> concurrent unsynchronized mutation of std::map -> data race (UB), map corruption or crash, and expired entries only sometimes removed.

findings.title: warm_cache spawns threads and never joins them (terminates process) and captures loop variable by reference
findings.description: Workers are created in a vector but the function returns without joining any of them, so std::thread's destructor calls std::terminate as soon as warm_cache returns. Each lambda also captures `&link` (a reference into the loop variable of the range-for over `links`) and `&cache` with no synchronization, so threads can outlive the vector and race on the Cache. This makes parallel warm-up unusable and can abort the whole process.

findings.title: stop_janitor only flips a flag: the janitor thread is never joined or deleted
findings.description: stop_janitor sets `g_running=false` but never joins `*g_janitor` and never frees it. The thread may still be sleeping inside sleep_for(interval) or traversing Store/Cache, so it can keep running past shutdown and access freed store/cache objects (use-after-free) and leak the thread and its heap allocation.

findings.title: Store has no synchronization while shared by janitor, handlers, and worker threads
findings.description: Link and quota maps are mutated and read by Store::create/resolve/rename/page/success_rate/remove/top/by_owner/extend/quotas/import_all/prune/total_hits and last_code without any mutex, even though they run concurrently (janitor sweep, HTTP handlers, warm_cache). Concurrent std::map access is a data race; create() returns a raw pointer into links_ and last_code() returns a string_view tied to map keys/temporaries, which become dangling once another thread erases or mutates the container.

findings.title: Cache is not thread-safe: concurrent get/set/erase/sweep/peek race on entries_ and hits_
findings.description: Cache::get, peek, set, erase, sweep and utilization access entries_ and hits_ with no synchronization while they are invoked concurrently by the janitor sweep, the resolver hot path and warm_cache threads. set() and erase()/sweep() also mutate the map during traversal. Interleaving two threads can corrupt entries_, lose entries, leak Entry* memory, and produce data races on long hits_.

findings.title: Authenticator mutates sessions_ without synchronization; verify returns a pointer into a live map
findings.description: issue()/verify()/revoke() read and write sessions_ concurrently (request handlers plus any janitor/admin use) with no lock, while verify() returns &pair.second pointing into a std::map that another thread can reallocate/erase, yielding a dangling reference and a data race. Additional concurrency hazard: std::rand() is used without synchronization to mint tokens.

findings.title: Metrics counters are non-atomic shared across request threads; errors_ is uninitialized
findings.description: Metrics is a single global object whose add_resolved/add_created and resolved()/created()/errors() read/increment plain longs from multiple request threads, a data race. errors_ is never initialized (constructors set resolved_/created_ to 0 but not errors_), so errors() also reads an indeterminate value even on one thread. Concurrent increments can be lost and compiled-out, corrupting dashboard stats.

findings.title: std::rand() used without synchronization in Store::create and Authenticator::issue
findings.description: Both Store::create (store.cpp:15) and Authenticator::issue (auth.cpp:22) call std::rand() to generate codes/tokens. std::rand maintains global mutable state and is not thread-safe in (at least) common implementations, so concurrent creation issues tokens/codes race on that state, producing nondeterministic or repeated values under load.

findings.title: Stack buffer overflow in bearer_token
findings.description: bearer_token copies an attacker-controlled Authorization header into a fixed 64-byte stack buffer with std::strcpy and no length check, then dereferences space+1 without checking for a space. An overlong header overflows the stack and corrupts control data; a header without a space makes space nullptr and crashes or reads invalid memory.

findings.title: Admin endpoint trusts client-controlled X-Admin header
findings.description: admin_quotas grants access solely when the request contains X-Admin: true, which any authenticated user can set. This bypasses the session/role check and exposes per-owner quota data.

findings.title: Path traversal via report name
findings.description: export_csv and read_report concatenate the user-supplied name into a filesystem path without sanitization or confinement. A name such as ../../etc/passwd lets an attacker write or read arbitrary files under the service account.

findings.title: Delete endpoint has no ownership or auth check
findings.description: delete_link removes any link by code taken from the query without consulting the authenticated session. Any user with a valid token can delete another user's (or any) short link.

findings.title: Expired sessions are not rejected
findings.description: verify returns a session even after expires_at has passed, so revoked-by-time tokens remain usable indefinitely and the 12-hour lifetime provides no protection.

findings.title: Session tokens minted with predictable std::rand
findings.description: issue generates tokens from std::rand, which is not cryptographically secure and may be unseeded/default. An attacker who can infer or observe a few tokens can predict new ones and hijack sessions.

findings.title: Permissive CORS with credentials
findings.description: respond sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This combination is unsafe and signals that credentialed cross-origin requests (and any token leakage) are intended to be allowed.

findings.title: Expired links remain resolvable
findings.description: resolve deletes a link when Clock::now() < expires_at (i.e. while still valid) and keeps it when expired, the opposite of intended. Expired/dead links therefore remain reachable.

findings.title: Open redirect via ?next=
findings.description: out sets Location to an unvalidated next parameter. An authenticated user (or attacker able to get a click) can steer victims to arbitrary URLs, including phishing destinations.

findings.title: Owner taken from query instead of session
findings.description: create_link uses owner from req.query rather than the authenticated session owner. A user can attribute links to another owner and exhaust/abuse that owner's quota (IDOR).

findings.title: Unknown token value leaked in 401 response
findings.description: The unauthorized response echoes the presented token back to the caller, disclosing a (possibly valid) secret to logs/browsers and aiding brute force.

findings.title: by_owner uses substring match and leaks nearby owners
findings.description: by_owner filters with owner.find(owner) != npos instead of equality, so querying 'a' returns every owner containing 'a', exposing other users' links.

findings.title: Weak unsalted password hash
findings.description: hash_password is a non-cryptographic djb2-style hash with no salt, making stored passwords trivially recoverable by lookup or brute force.

findings.title: Hardcoded fallback secret when LINKD_SECRET unset
findings.description: If LINKD_SECRET is missing, the service uses the publicly known 'dev-secret-do-not-use', allowing anyone to forge/verify against the predictable secret in misconfigured deployments.

findings.title: Export files rely on umask for confidentiality
findings.description: The report purportedly service-user-only is written with default file permissions, so on a typical umask (022) other users on the box can read it.

findings.title: Predictable /tmp snapshot path TOCTOU
findings.description: write_snapshot writes to a fixed /tmp/linkd-snapshot.json then renames, allowing a local attacker to pre-create or swap that path (symlink attack) and to win a TOCTOU race.
